data.title: Tech Stack
data.tagline: The set of languages, frameworks, data services, and tools used to build and run software
data.learningOutcome: You can separate the jobs of building a page, styling it, and running a site in a small project.
data.description: A website might combine JavaScript, React, a database, build tools, and hosting. They handle different jobs: page behavior, interface, data, and operation. Start by learning what the project already uses before replacing several layers at once.

learning.assumes: You know a web page can open, accept input, and respond to clicks.
learning.outcome: You can separate the jobs of building a page, styling it, and running a site in a small project.

explanation.title: Write the content
explanation.text: The page needs source files before a browser can show anything.

explanation.title: Connect the roles
explanation.text: Some tools organize the page, some set spacing and color, and others start it on a computer or server.

explanation.title: Use only what fits
explanation.text: A combination that opens, responds, and ships the current project is enough.

data.boundary: A tech stack is not a required shopping list. A common beginner-friendly full-stack for vibe coding is: Next.js (framework) + Tailwind CSS (styling) + shadcn/ui (components) + Supabase (database) + Vercel (hosting), but the right stack depends on the project needs.

lessonPractice.title: An Agent proposes replacing a project's UI, data service, and deployment with popular tools before inspecting the code. What should happen first?

options.label: Inventory current languages, frameworks, data services, and runtime before judging replacement value
options.feedback: A stack describes actual responsibilities, and only current constraints make replacement cost and outcome comparable.

options.label: Replace every layer by popularity first and resolve migration and compatibility afterward
options.feedback: Changing many layers expands risk and diagnosis scope, while popularity does not prove fit.

options.label: List product names without saying which one owns UI, data, or deployment
options.feedback: A brand list hides responsibilities, so overlaps, gaps, and replacement impact cannot be judged.

data.agentPrompt: Inspect project configuration and map the current stack by UI, interaction, data, backend, and deployment responsibilities. Replace nothing yet; for each proposal state the problem, migration scope, compatibility risk, and verifiable benefit.
